checklist.detail: Chamber pressure 1.10 MPa is unusually high for a pressure-fed design - classic real examples (Apollo SPS, LM descent/ascent engine, R-4D) cluster at 0.7-0.8 MPa. Only modern composite-overwrapped tank technology (e.g. SpaceX SuperDraco, ~6.9 MPa) reaches this high, implying a much heavier/higher-tech tank than this tool models.

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~6.0), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~6.2 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.0 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~2.9 mm channel width, this reversed ~6.1 MPa differential is ~102 MPa against a ~67 MPa allowable (Stainless Steel (304/316), SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
